reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Started again with the adopted TER credit tables, the dated common-core and Politics curriculum nodes, individual course contents and entry rules, and active UCR profiles or descriptions. Reconsidered the exact finished concepts, schedules, partial relationships and reader-facing fields from those underlying sources rather than treating the earlier diagnosis or validators as academic approval. This is a separate analytical pass by the same AI, not an independent person.
findings: The adopted curriculum lists Politics first; this confirms the prior neutral selection without reference to UCR fit. Seventeen core courses total 102 EC, nine Politics courses total 54, the thesis twelve and electives twelve. Counted only the common curriculum and Politics nodes, excluding parallel majors and the designated-elective list from the required total. The 27 course entries and one open component form sixty EC per year, with no parent/child double counting.

The ten first-year courses supply sixty EC, meeting the 54-EC continuation threshold and completing all later named course/major prerequisites. Law and Behaviour requires LJM I, an alias for the first-year Law, Justice and Morality course. The second economics, politics/governance and psychology courses follow their first-year foundations. Statistical Analysis precedes the recommended political-methods course; Research Lab follows prior methods. No Economics/Business mathematics-test rule is imposed on Politics.

Research Lab is a separate proposal/design module, not thesis credit. The individual interdisciplinary thesis has an 8,000–10,000-word report and mandatory presentation/defence in Year-3 Semester 2. Entry is 120 EC excluding electives before that semester; both earlier years alone supply 120. The first-semester major courses and two elective slots, followed by the spring core/methods/behaviour/thesis courses, total sixty in the final year. Open electives may require approval; an internship is optional and is not instantiated. Non-credit What You Don’t Learn in School remains separate.

The course descriptions establish social psychology, economic reasoning and macroeconomics, empirical methods, EU politics, international relations, democracy, public policy and political theory. Sixteen partial relationships identify important shared content; unequal EC weights do not preclude them. Constitutional comparison provides the formal-institutions part of Politics/Power/Governance I; civil-society solidarity provides a social-theory counterpart to the integrated psychology/economics seminar; econometrics provides the quantitative part of the political-methods course. Their limits are explicit. Research Lab and the thesis are not matched to generic academic skills.

The closest UCR response has actual sustained political, psychological, legal and economic substance, strengthened with political thought, policy, constitutional law, human rights and organisational psychology. Behavioural public policy is differentiated through computational analysis, negotiation and ethics, not an unsupported claim of more psychology than the closest plan. The legal response provides a distinct sustained doctrinal sequence plus normative and qualitative inquiry. Broad philosophical, clinical or mathematical substitutes were not allowed to displace the target’s defining substance.

All sixty-six target interests were reconciled, including support-only topics and search-only examples/outcomes. Current alumni destinations are illustrations subject to admissions, not academic or career entitlements; historical individual outcomes do not generate UCR options. Every selected course contribution was reconsidered independently of shared description approval. All schedules pass current offerings and formal prerequisites, first-year PPD and advanced-course requirements. Pairwise differences are thirty, fifty-two-and-a-half and fifty-two-and-a-half EC each way.

Read all twenty-eight external titles, ten note anchors, three concepts, sixteen partial relationships, twelve unmatched reasons, audience references and thirty-three selected UCR descriptions against the established renderer mapping. The specific current-politics seminar and cultural psychology content retain meaningful gaps. Exact cached prose and provenance reviews are reused only where unchanged. Optional independent research is parallel to the actual thesis and outside scheduled credits. No application or renderer behaviour changed; no live rendering, modal or runtime test is claimed.
